ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r2.claim: The wording suggests the blind man’s arrival dismayed the Prophet because he feared it would offend Quraysh vanity, although he was neglecting a more worthy student.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r2.anchor: he had become indifferent to a true student

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r3.claim: The messengers’ mission is to purify followers spiritually; those seeking reform deserve attention, while people without that urge do not advance the preaching mission despite worldly importance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r3.anchor: the real objective of the messengers of God is to spiritually purify their followers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r4.claim: The earnest seeker is marked by a desire for inner purification and by benefiting from reminders.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r4.anchor: he is desirous of his inner-purification and he is one who benefits from being reminded

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r1.claim: True students either come with a question and seek guidance or come to hear instruction and learn from answers to others; either purpose makes them worthy of attention.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r1.anchor: there were two types of people among them: one, people who had a question regarding their instruction and training

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r2.claim: People who come only to be pampered should stay home and await their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r2.anchor: As far as people who want to be pampered are concerned, they should sit at home

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r6.claim: He says لعله might refer to the disbeliever whom the Prophet hoped would accept Islam; Abu Hayyan rejects this as unworthy Qur'anic interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p406/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقيل: الضمير في لعله للكافر، يعني أنك طمعت في أن يتزكى بالإسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r1.claim: The apparent analysis treats laʿalla like an interrogative because both convey a request and permit suspension: the sense is that he does not know whether purification or remembrance is hoped for.
SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r1.anchor: الظاهر إجراء الترجي مجرى الاستفهام لما بينهما من معنى الطلب في التعليق؛ لأن المعنى منصب على تسلط الدراية على الترجي

SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r2.claim: Another pause analysis stops at يدري, then starts a new question about who can inform the Prophet of the man’s situation and outcome, followed by ‘perhaps he will purify himself.’
SAMIN-DURR:80:3/r2.anchor: وقيل: الوقف على " يدري " والابتداء بما بعده على معنى: وما يطلعك على أمره وعاقبة حاله، ثم ابتدأ فقال:

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r1.claim: The shift to direct address reassures the Prophet after the preceding rebuke, replacing estrangement with attention and turning toward him after turning away.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r1.anchor: لما فيه من الإيناس بعد الإيحاش والإقبال بعد الإعراض

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r2.claim: Calling Ibn Umm Maktum the blind man highlights his excuse for interrupting the Prophet's speech while he was occupied with the people, and invites compassion toward him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r2.anchor: للأشعار بعذره في الإقدام على قطع كلام الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r3.claim: Another explanation sees the initial third-person wording followed by direct address as heightened censure, like publicly complaining and then confronting the offender with blame and proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r3.anchor: وقيل إن الغيبة أولا والخطاب ثانيا لزيادة الإنكار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r4.claim: The description also hints that every weak person deserves the consideration shown to someone in his condition, rather than restricting the lesson to this particular blind man.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r4.anchor: وفيه أيضا دفع إيهام الإختصاص بالأعمى المعين وإيماء إلى أن كل ضعيف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r5.claim: With an elided causal lām, the phrase modifies the first verb for Kufans, the second for Basrans, and both for al-Farra; all agree it gives the cause of both actions in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r5.anchor: وهو معمول لأول الفعلين على مختار الكوفيين وثانيهما على مختار البصريين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads ʿabasa with a doubled bāʾ for intensification, not to make the form causative.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r6.anchor: قرأ زيد بن علي على عبس بتشديد الباء للمبالغة لا للتعدية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r7.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمران الجوني وعيسى وبعض القراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Imran al-Jawni, and Isa read with one hamza, while some readers use two articulated hamzas; in both readings the hamza is an interrogative of repudiation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r7.anchor: والحسن وأبو عمران الجوني وعيسى آن بهمزة بعدها وبعض القراء بهمزتين محققتين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r8.claim: A pause is made at tawalla, and the sense is an elliptical exception: except that the blind man came, then the rebuke is directed accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r8.anchor: والهمزة في القراءتين للأستفهام الأنكاري ويوقف على تولي والمعنى إلا أن جاء الأعمى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r9.claim: The pronoun in laʿallahu refers to the blind man, and the clause appears to attach to the verb of knowing as its object: what could make you know that he may purify himself?
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r9.anchor: وضمير لعله للأعمى والظاهر أن الجملة متعلقة بفعل الدراية على وجه سد مسد مفعوله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r10.claim: Purification here is his cleansing himself of some traces of sin through the religious teachings he learns.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p39#3/r10.anchor: أي أي شيء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى لعله يتطهر بما يتلقن من الشرائع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r2.claim: The Prophet does not know whether the man would purify himself or remember; the verse denies such foreknowledge, since knowing the outcome would have prevented what happened.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r2.anchor: والمعنى أنك لا تدري ما هو مترقب منه من ترك أو تذكر ولو دريت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r3.claim: The hope may belong to the blind man or to the Prophet; even a reasonable hope that he would purify himself was enough to forbid frowning and turning away, especially given his demonstrated receptiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r3.anchor: والترجي راجع إلى الأعمى أو إلى النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r4.claim: The purification is treated as something hoped for rather than certain, so the term can denote some purification rather than complete purification; the wording gives the basic sense without requiring perfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r4.anchor: اعتبر متعلق التزكي بعض الأوضار ترشيحا لذلك وفيه إظهار ما يقتضي مقام العظمة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r5.claim: Some take the omitted object of ma yudrika to be the man's affair and final state; the following clause then resumes and explains the hint that he has an important, divinely known prospect.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم متعلق الدراية محذوف أي ما يدريك أمره وعاقبة حاله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r6.claim: On that analysis purification can mean total cleansing from sin, while remembering can benefit him if he does not attain complete purification; the author calls a further proposed distinction between obligatory and optional learning weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r6.anchor: أي لعله يتطهر بما يقتبس منك من أوضار الأثم بالكلية أو يتذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r7.claim: The passage indirectly suggests that the disbelievers receiving the Prophet's attention were not expected to purify themselves, as in telling a poor learner that perhaps another, capable listener will understand.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r7.anchor: وفي الآية تعريض وإشعار بأن من تصدى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لتزكيتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r8.claim: A further view says the alluded person was already purified from sins and receptive to admonition.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r8.anchor: وقيل جاء التعريض من جهة أن المحدث عنه كان متزكيا من الآثام متعظا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r9.claim: Some make the pronoun refer to the disbeliever, with hope attributed to the Prophet, who hoped for his conversion and so turned from the blind man; al-Alusi rejects this because the disbeliever was not previously mentioned and the pronoun is singular despite the group addressed, though a report says the person was one.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40/r9.anchor: وقيل ضمير لعله للكافر والترجي راجع إلى الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r1.claim: The clause “what makes you know?” is circumstantial in relation to the preceding passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r1.anchor: وجملة { وما يدريك } الخ في موضع الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r2.claim: The formula combines interrogative mā with causative darā; it means “what makes you know?” and is like “what made you know?” in 69:3 or “what makes you perceive?” in 6:109.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r2.anchor: ( وما يدريك ) مركبة من ( ما ) الاستفهامية وفعل الدراية المقترن بهمزة التعدية ، أي ما يجعلك داريا أي عالما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r3.claim: These formulas alert the hearer to something overlooked, begin with generality, and then detail it, as in 101:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r3.anchor: والاستفهام في هذه التراكيب مراد منه التنبيه على مغفول عنه ثم تقع بعده جملة نحو ما أدراك ما القارعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r4.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r4.claim: Al-Raghib says that whenever the Quran uses “what made you know,” it gives an explanation afterward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : ما ذكر ما أدراك في القرآن إلا وذكر بيانه بعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r5.claim: The explanation may be explicit, as here and in 97:2–3, or the following wording may instead convey awe, as in 101:10 and 69:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r5.anchor: فقد يبينه تفصيل مثل قوله هنا : { وما يدريك لعله يزكى } وقوله : { وما أدراك ما ليلة القدر ليلة القدر خير من ألف شهر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r6.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi holds that laʿalla suspends the governance of verbs of the heart because hope, like interrogation, expresses a request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r6.anchor: فإن ( لعل ) من موجبات تعليق أفعال القلوب على ما أثبته أبو علي الفارسي في ( التذكرة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r7.claim: With its object governance suspended, يدريك no longer takes three objects; the causative form leaves it with one, and the following clause is independent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r7.anchor: صار غير متعد إلى ثلاثة مفاعيل وبقي متعديا إلى مفعول واحد بهمزة التعدية التي فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r9.claim: The man may gain further purification if guided: faith can deepen and lead to good deeds, adding the law’s virtues and noble character beyond initial belief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r9.anchor: فالمراد ب ( يتزكى ) تزكية زائدة على تزكية الإيمان بالتملي بفضائل شرائعه ومكارم أخلاقه مما يفيضه هديك عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr quotes the Prophet saying that if his companions remained as they were with him after leaving, angels would shake their hands; he uses it as an example of guidance increasing believers’ spiritual rank.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p105/r10.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لو أنكم تكونون إذا خرجتم من عندي كما تكونون عندي لصافحتكم الملائكة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r1.claim: The clause wa-mā yudrīka and what follows is syntactically a circumstantial clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r1.anchor: وجملة { وما يدريك } الخ في موضع الحال .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r2.claim: The phrase combines interrogative mā with causative adrā, meaning what makes you know; it parallels mā adrāka and mā yushʿirukum, as in 69:3 and 6:109.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r2.anchor: ( وما يدريك ) مركبة من ( ما ) الاستفهامية وفعل الدراية المقترن بهمزة التعدية ، أي ما يجعلك داريا أي عالما .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r3.claim: Such interrogatives alert the listener to something overlooked, then introduce a following clause that first leaves the matter general and then elaborates it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r3.anchor: والاستفهام في هذه التراكيب مراد منه التنبيه على مغفول عنه ثم تقع بعده جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r4.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib says every Qur'anic occurrence of mā adrāka is followed by an explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : ما ذكر ما أدراك في القرآن إلا وذكر بيانه بعده ا ه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says the following explanation may clarify the matter, as in 97:2–3, or intensify its mystery, as in 101:10 and 69:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r5.anchor: قلت : فقد يبينه تفصيل مثل قوله هنا : { وما يدريك لعله يزكى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r6.claim: Following Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, laʿalla suspends the heart-verb yudrīka from governing its two objects because hope, like interrogation, is a request; the following clause is independent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r6.anchor: فإن ( لعل ) من موجبات تعليق أفعال القلوب على ما أثبته أبو علي الفارسي في ( التذكرة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r8.claim: The hoped-for purification is growth beyond faith: guidance can root faith more firmly and lead the blind believer to many good deeds and the virtues of the law and noble character.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r8.anchor: فالمراد ب ( يتزكى ) تزكية زائدة على تزكية الإيمان بالتملي بفضائل شرائعه ومكارم أخلاقه مما يفيضه هديك عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r9.claim: The Prophet says that if the believers remained after leaving him as they were in his presence, angels would shake hands with them; Ibn ʿĀshūr uses this to illustrate increased spiritual rank.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#5/r9.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لو أنكم تكونون إذا خرجتم من عندي كما تكونون عندي لصافحتكم الملائكة )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r1.claim: The Prophet heard Aisha describe a woman as short and replied that she had said a word which, if mixed into the sea, would contaminate it; mentioning people to belittle them is backbiting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r1.anchor: وقد سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عائشة تذكر امرأة، فقالت: إنها القصيرة. فقال لها: لقد قلت كلمة لو مزجت بالبحر لمزجته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r2.claim: The Prophet is told that he cannot know the man's eventual state; perhaps he will be purified, grow in blessing, and benefit from faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r2.anchor: أي وما يطلعك على أمره وعقبى حاله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r3.claim: يزكى derives from يتزكى with tāʾ assimilated into zāy; the same applies to يذكر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r3.anchor: وأصل يزكى: يتزكى، فأدغم التاء في الزاي وكذلك يذكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#2/r1.claim: He might cleanse himself of sins through good works and what he learns from you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#2/r1.anchor: أي يتطهر من الذنوب بالعمل الصالح وما يتعلمه منك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#2/r2.claim: Muqatil says the meaning is that he might believe.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.claim: They say it was revealed when Ibn Umm Maktūm interrupted the Prophet's effort to convert Meccan leaders; the Prophet turned back to them and God rebuked him.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم أتى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored him, welcomed him as the man over whom his Lord reproached him, and asked his needs.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.anchor: فكان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعد ذلك يكرمه، وإذا رآه قال: مرحبا بمن عاتبني ربي فيه،

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.speaker: أنس
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya in armor with a black banner.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.anchor: قال أنس: رأيته يوم القادسية، عليه درع، ومعه راية سوداء.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd relates the saying that if the Messenger concealed revelation, he would have concealed this passage.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان يقال: لو كتم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - شيئا من الوحي لكتم هذا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r12.claim: The question means: what could make you know the blind man’s true state?
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r12.anchor: { وما يدريك } وأي شيء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r13.claim: One reading takes the pronoun as the blind man: he may purify himself by learning religious law and shedding sin, or take admonition that helps him obey; the Prophet could not know what might follow.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r13.anchor: أي يتطهر بما يتلقن من الشرائع من بعض أوضار الإثم ( { أو يذكر } أو يتعظ { فتنفعه } ذكراك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r14.claim: Another reading takes the pronoun as the unbeliever: the Prophet hoped Islam and the reminder would bring him toward truth, though he could not know that this would happen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r14.anchor: وقيل : الضمير في { لعله } للكافر . يعني أنك طمعت في أن يتزكى بالإسلام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r1.claim: The rhetorical question asks what could make the Prophet know the blind man's condition.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r1.anchor: وأى شىء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r2.claim: The blind man might purify himself by hearing the Prophet and shedding the stain of ignorance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r2.anchor: لعل الاعمى يتطهر بما يسمع منك من دنس الجهل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r3.claim: Yazakkā derives from yatazakkā, with tāʾ assimilated into zāy.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317/r3.anchor: وأصله يتزكى فأدغمت التاء فى الزاى وكذا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#2/r5.claim: The Prophet cannot know whether the man will purify himself or take heed; knowing that prospect would have prevented his neglect.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#2/r5.anchor: أى انك لا تدى ما هو مترقب منه من تزك أو تذكر ولو دريت لما فرط ذلك منك

BURSEVI:v10p258/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258/r1.claim: Direct address intensifies the reproach, like a complainant turning to confront the person who wronged him; no one could make the Prophet know the man’s inner state.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r1.anchor: لذلك فإن المشافهة أدخل في تشديد العتبا كمن يشكو إلى الناس جانيا جنى عليه ثم يقبل على الجاني

BURSEVI:v10p258/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258/r2.claim: A pause is appropriate after this question: what follows is a new statement, not its object.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r2.anchor: أي لا يدريك شيء فتم الكلام عنده فيوقف عليه وليس ما بعده مفعوله بل هو ابتداء كلام

BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.claim: Al-Suhaylī observes that the passage first reports the incident in third person, then turns to direct address, mirroring the Prophet’s initial turning away before addressing him to console him.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r3.anchor: قال الامام السهيلي رحمه الله ، انظر كيف نزلت الآية بلفظ الأخبار عن الغائب

BURSEVI:v10p258/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r4.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p258/r4.claim: Al-Suhaylī says the Prophet hoped for the conversion of the pagan, identified as al-Walīd or Umayya, whose Islam might have brought many others to Islam.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r4.anchor: وهو الوليد أو أمية وكان مثله يسلم بإسلامه بشر كثير فكلم نبيه عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v10p258/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r5.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p258/r5.claim: Al-Suhaylī notes that Ibn Umm Maktūm was already Muslim and had learned his religious essentials, while the pagans had not accepted Islam.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r5.anchor: وأما أولئك الكفار فما كانوا قد أسلموا وكان إسلامهم سببا لإسلام جمع عظيم

BURSEVI:v10p258/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258/r6.claim: Even if the Prophet sought a greater benefit, his action outwardly suggested preferring the rich and disregarding the poor man’s hurt, so God reproached him for leaving the better course.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r6.anchor: إلا أن ظاهر ما فعله الرسول عليه السلام يوهم تقديم الأغنياء على الفقراء وقلة المبالاة بانكسار قلوب الفقراء

BURSEVI:v10p258/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258/r7.claim: Yazzakkā is contracted from yatazakkā and means that the blind man may purify himself through what he learns from the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r7.anchor: بتشديدين أصله يتزكى أي يتطهر بما يقتبس منك من أوضار الأوزار

BURSEVI:v10p258/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258/r8.claim: Although God knows the outcome, laʿalla in speech of the mighty can express certainty; alternatively it conveys hope from the Prophet’s perspective to stress that neglecting a hoped-for seeker is impermissible.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r8.anchor: وكلمة لعل مع تحقق التزكي وارد على سنن الكبرياء فإن لعل في كلام العظماء يراد به القطع والتحقيق

BURSEVI:v10p258/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258/r11.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v10p258/r11.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that the Prophet could not know whether the man would attain purification or recollection; if he had known, he would not have neglected him.
BURSEVI:v10p258/r11.anchor: المعنى إنك لا تدري ما هو مترقب منه من تزكى أو تذكر ولو دريت لما فرط ذلك منك

RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r1.speaker: القول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r1.claim: The first view takes the pronoun to the blind man: what he learns may cleanse ignorance or sin, or admonish him and help him obey.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r1.anchor: الأول : أي شيء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى لعله يتطهر بما يتلقن منك

RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r2.speaker: القول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r2.claim: The second view takes the pronoun to the disbeliever: perhaps he will accept Islam, or the reminder will bring him nearer to accepting truth, though you cannot know this will happen.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن الضمير في لعله للكافر ، بمعنى أنت طمعت في أن يزكى الكافر بالإسلام

TABRISI:80:20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r6.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, also named Abdullah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik ibn Rabiʿa al-Fihri, when he came as the Prophet was urging Quraysh leaders toward Islam.
TABRISI:80:20/r6.anchor: قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك ابن ربيعة الفهري

TABRISI:80:20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r7.claim: The Prophet was speaking with ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAbbas, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked to be taught; the Prophet turned away, thinking the leaders might scorn a following of blind people and slaves.
TABRISI:80:20/r7.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام والعباس بن عبد المطلب وأبيا وأمية ابني خلف

TABRISI:80:20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:80:20/r8.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, greeted him as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and appointed him deputy in Medina twice.
TABRISI:80:20/r8.anchor: وكان رسول الله بعد ذلك يكرمه

TABRISI:80:20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:80:20/r9.claim: Anas ibn Malik says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black standard.
TABRISI:80:20/r9.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك: فرأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع ومعه راية سوداء

TABRISI:80:20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r10.speaker: المرتضى علم الهدى
TABRISI:80:20/r10.claim: Al-Murtada rejects identifying the passage's subject as the Prophet: the text does not name him, and frowning at a believing seeker or preferring rich people to the poor conflicts with his noble character.
TABRISI:80:20/r10.anchor: قال المرتضى علم الهدى قدس الله روحه: ليس في ظاهر الآية دلالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says yazzakkā means to become upright and do good.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra relates purification to the knowledge the blind man wanted to learn from the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: أي بما أراد أن يتعلمه من علمك (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r3.claim: The preferred sense is purifying oneself from sins through good deeds and benefiting from what one learns from the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى: يتطهر من الذنوب بالعمل الصالح، والانتفاع بما يتعلم منك.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد وعطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r4.claim: Some commentators take it as purification from polytheism through Islam; the author rejects this because Ibn Umm Maktum had already believed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p211#2/r4.anchor: وذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أن المعنى: يتطهر من الشرك بالإسلام. وهو قول: ابن زيد (¬1)، (ومعنى قول عطاء) (¬2) (¬3). والصحيح هو الأول

TAB-FULL:v24p105/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r3.claim: The blind man might purify himself from his sins.
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r3.anchor: وما يدريك يا محمد، لعل هذا الأعمى الذي عبست في وجهه يزكى: يقول: يتطهر من ذنوبه

TAB-FULL:v24p105/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p105/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses يزكى as becoming Muslim.

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.claim: The sūra rebukes preferring the wealthy and privileged to poor believers, then recalls human dependence on God's care despite ingratitude and turns to resurrection, recompense, and warning.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r4.anchor: فغرض السورة عتاب من يقدم الأغنياء والمترفين على الضعفاء والمساكين من المؤمنين فيرفع أهل الدنيا ويضع أهل الآخرة

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r8.claim: The clause beginning “what will make you know” is circumstantial to the subject of “frowned and turned away.”

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r9.claim: Tazakkā means becoming pure through good action after reflection; the reflection is taking heed and awakening to true belief.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r9.anchor: والمراد بالتزكي التطهر بعمل صالح بعد التذكر الذي هو الاتعاظ والانتباه للاعتقاد الحق

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.claim: The first two verses speak in the third person, distancing the rebuke; the next two switch to direct address, intensifying reproach and accountability.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r11.anchor: ويزيد شدة بإتيان الآيتين الأوليين في سياق الغيبة لما فيه من الإعراض عن المشافهة والدلالة على تشديد الإنكار

TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.claim: On the view that the Prophet is the one reproached, third-person wording honors him by implying someone else acted; the later direct address also honors him through intimacy after estrangement.
TABATABAI:80:1-4/r13.anchor: وقيل - بناء على كون المراد بالمعاتب هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - أن في التعبير عنه أولا بضمير الغيبة إجلالا له

TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.claim: Al-Majmaʿ recounts that Abdullah ibn Shurayḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihri, Ibn Umm Maktūm, interrupted the Prophet's appeal to ʿUtba, Abū Jahl, al-ʿAbbās, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf to ask for teaching; the Prophet frowned, fearing the elites would scorn followers who were blind or enslaved, then turned back to them.
TABATABAI:80:13-16/r12.anchor: في المجمع قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك بن ربيعة الفهروي

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.claim: The blind man might become purified through good works and learning, or remember and heed Qurʾanic admonition so that the reminder benefits his religion.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r8.anchor: أي لعل هذا الأعمى { يزكى } يتطهر بالعمل الصالح

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r9.claim: God shows great courtesy: He does not directly say “you frowned,” but shifts to direct address only after passing over the frown.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r9.anchor: وفي هذا لطف من الله عظيم لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ لم يخاطبه في باب العبوس

THALABI:v10p130#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p130#3/r6.claim: The blind man might purify himself of sins, take admonition, and reform.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r6.anchor: أي يتطهر من ذنوبه ويتعظ ويصلح

THALABI:v10p130#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p130#3/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the hoped-for purification as accepting Islam.

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r8.claim: The one seeking guidance may be purified by remembering what he learns from the Prophet.

ITQAN:v2p504#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r3.claim: Laʿalla can also be interrogative, as shown by its use with verbs meaning know or perceive.
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r3.anchor: الثالث الاستفهام وخرج عليه ﴿ لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا ﴾

FARRA:v3p235/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r4.claim: The blind man may have purified himself through what he wanted to learn from the Prophet's teaching.
FARRA:v3p235/r4.anchor: بما أراد أن يتعلمه من علمك

FARRA:v3p235/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p235/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p235/r5.claim: After this revelation the Prophet treated Ibn Umm Maktūm with care and honor, even appointing him to lead the prayer.
FARRA:v3p235/r5.anchor: وأكرمه بعد هذه الآية حتى استخلفه على الصلاة

NAHHAS:v5p149/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p149/r5.claim: The underlying form يتزكى assimilates its tāʾ into zāy.
NAHHAS:v5p149/r5.anchor: والأصل يتزكى أدغمت في التاء في الزاي

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.claim: ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.anchor: There is no basic difference between the central theme of both sūrahs.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r1.claim: He might purify himself from sins through good deeds and what he learns from the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r1.anchor: يتطهر من الذنوب بالعمل الصالح وما يتعلمه منك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the word means that he may accept Islam.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r1.claim: The question means, how could you know his state? He may purify himself from sins by what he learns from you; this hints that the Prophet turned away to help another become purified.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r1.anchor: وأي شيء يجعلك داريا بحاله لعله يتطهر من الآثام بما يتلقف منك

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r3.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the unbeliever: the Prophet hoped to purify and admonish him by conversion, and so turned from the other man, though success was uncertain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r3.anchor: وقيل الضمير في { لعله } للكافر أي أنك طمعت في تزكيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r9.claim: No one can know the states of hearts except God, however diligently a person tries to discern them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r9.anchor: فإن ذوات الصدور لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r10.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm may be purified and grow in goodness through what he hears, even if only to a slight degree.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r10.anchor: بحيث يرجى تطهره ونمو أحواله الصالحة بما يسمع منك ولوعلى أدنى الوجوه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm gained an immense, lasting reputation from this event, unlike Pharaoh, who was turned away and neither purified himself nor benefited from the reminder.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r1.anchor: فيا له صيتا ما أجله بخلاف من قدم ذكره ممن طرد فلم يتزك ولم ينتفع بالذكرى حين قصد بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r1.claim: Yazakkā derives from yatazakkā: tāʾ changes to zāy because their articulation points are close, enabling assimilation; yadhdhakkaru has a similar assimilation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r1.anchor: و { يزكى } أصله : يتزكى ، قلبت التاء زايا لتقارب مخرجيهما قصدا ليتأتى الإدغام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r2.claim: Tazakkī is the reflexive result of purification: its effect comes about in the person; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes its earlier discussion in al-Nāziʿāt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r2.anchor: والتزكي : مطاوع زكاه ، أي يحصل أثر التزكية في نفسه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r1.claim: Yazakkā derives from yatazakkā: tāʾ changes to zāy because their articulation points are close, enabling assimilation; yadhdhakkaru has a similar assimilation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r1.anchor: و { يزكى } أصله : يتزكى ، قلبت التاء زايا لتقارب مخرجيهما قصدا ليتأتى الإدغام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r2.claim: Tazakkī is the reflexive result of purification: its effect comes about in the person; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes its earlier discussion in al-Nāziʿāt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r2.anchor: والتزكي : مطاوع زكاه ، أي يحصل أثر التزكية في نفسه .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r2.claim: The blind man might attain inner purification, or be admonished and deterred from forbidden acts so that the reminder benefits him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r2.anchor: أي: يحصل له زكاة وطهارة في نفسه. (أو يذكر فتنفعه الذكرى) أي: يحصل له اتعاظ وانزجار عن المحارم،

JISHUMI:v10p7279/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r9.claim: Yazzakkā derives from yatazakkā by assimilating tāʾ into zāy; yadhdhakkaru similarly derives from yatadhakkaru, while tazkiyah means purification and tadhakkur seeking a reminder.
JISHUMI:v10p7279/r9.anchor: يزكى: أصله يتزكى فأدغمت التاء في الزاي، كما أدغمت في (يذكر)

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r8.claim: The blind man might purify himself through good deeds and avoiding sins, or remember God’s signs and benefit from that remembrance.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r8.anchor: أي: لا تدري (لعله يزكى) يتطهر بالأعمال الصالحة، والتجنب من الذنوب والقبائح أو يذكر أي: يذكر آيات الله،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r7.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r7.claim: It can mean to worship through good deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r7.anchor: يتعبد بالأعمال الصالحة ، قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r8.claim: It can mean to memorize the Quran being recited to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r8.anchor: يحفظ ما يتلوه عليه من القرآن ، قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r9.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r9.claim: It can mean to gain understanding of religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p202#2/r9.anchor: يتفقه في الدين , قاله ابن شجرة

MUQATIL:80:1-7/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r4.claim: The blind man might believe and pray, being reminded in the Qur’an of what he had corrupted.
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r4.anchor: يقول: لعله أن يؤمن فيصلى فيتذكر في القرآن بما قد أفسد

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r3.claim: On the primary reading, “he” is Ibn Umm Maktum, who may be purified by the Qur'an and religious instruction, gaining purity and losing ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r3.anchor: { لعله } يعني ابن أم مكتوم { يزكى } بما استدعى منك تعليمه إياه من القرآن والدين

QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, “he” refers to the unbeliever: the Prophet hoped he might accept Islam, but could not know whether that hope would come true.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:1-4#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في «لعله» للكافر يعني إنك إذا طمعت في أن يتزكى بالإسلام أو يذكر
